To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the experimental training improved subjects’ task performance and that the retrospective pre-test-posttest design is a more valid approach than the conventional pretestposttest design to detect these effects.
(1) the experimental training in seeing problems is effective in changing task performance and that (2) the retrospective pretest design controls for the effect of the response-shift phenomenon.

(a) the experimental training in the use of a specific problem-solving strategy is effective in improving subjects task performance; (b) the traditional pre-post comparison does not reflect this actual improvement in task performance; (c) the retrospective self-report pretest-posttest is a valid alternative in measuring the effect of the training.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem that the conventional pretest design is inadequate to detect changes in performance due to training, and that the retrospective approach provides a valid alternative.
the question of how to evaluate the effects of training programs on self-reported measures of behavior.
the problem of the response-shift in the pretest-posttest paradigm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the retrospective pre-test-post-test design is a valid alternative to the conventional design when self-reports are the outcome criterion.
the retrospective pretests are superior to conventional pretests, because of the fact that they control for the response-shift phenomenon.

both the conventional and retrospective pretest-post-test approach are equally valid when the researcher is interested in the effect of an experimental training program on the subjects’ self-report measures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pretest-posttest approach, as well as the retrospective pretest approach, is a valid and useful method for the evaluation of educational training.
a retrospective pretest-post-test design is a valid means for measuring change.
the retrospective pre-test is an effective tool in educational research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retrospective pre-test is a valid and useful tool to assess the effects of interventions.
it is possible to improve the quality of research by using the retrospective pretest in the pre-post design.
retrospective pretesting can be used to assess the effectiveness of interventions in the educational training context, as well as in other domains.
